risk.line: HIGH, held for a TWENTY-FOURTH consecutive pass. The ship struck in Hormuz late Saturday is now named by Iranian state media as an Iranian cargo vessel off Qeshm, with one crew member dead - which reads as enforcement of the US blockade rather than a spoiler before Monday's Oman talks, though nobody has claimed it. Saudi jets flew more than 100 raids in 48 hours on the Houthi-held coast and the approaches to Marib, and a Russian strike landed 800 metres from Poland. CRIT still requires an American killed or an American hull hit, and neither has been reported.

forecasts.q: Abdulraof Macacua, the Manila-appointed interim Chief Minister running as an independent, is elected Chief Minister by the first regular Bangsamoro Parliament before 31 December 2026
forecasts.note: OPENED at 50, paying a Southeast Asia coverage debt carried for seven sessions, the day before the region's first regular parliamentary vote. The scored object is the veto player, not the ballot: the Chief Minister is chosen by the Parliament, so the question is whether Manila's appointee can turn incumbency into a parliamentary majority against the MILF's own party machine, led by its chairman Murad Ebrahim, whom Marcos replaced with Macacua in March 2025. BASE RATE: every elected regional governor of the old ARMM from 1996 to 2013 was aligned with the sitting President, which alone would put this near 70. Held to 50 because this is the first PARLIAMENTARY selection, where the MILF's organisational discipline matters more than patronage, and because Macacua must first win a contested district after an unexplained ambush on his convoy in August. The two frameworks - Hutchcroft's patronage state and the rebel-to-party literature, where the movement's cohesion is the variable - point opposite ways, hence Low. Single limb. Kill: he loses his seat (to 3); the UBJP wins an outright majority (to 25).

forecasts.q: The US House passes the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (or a version of it) on a recorded floor vote before 31 October 2026
forecasts.note: OPENED at 58, twenty points under the base rate on purpose. Senate-passed sanctions bills with veto-proof margins usually clear the House - CAATSA went through 419-3 in 2017 - and this one passed the Senate 86-11 with the White House reported in favour. It is held down by three named constraints: Speaker Johnson needs near-unanimous Republican support on the procedural rule and it is unclear he has it; senior Democrats Meeks, Neal and Beyer object that it expands presidential tariff power, so a cross-party rescue is not guaranteed; and the pre-midterm calendar means a slipped week is close to a dead bill. Framework: Krehbiel's pivotal politics - supermajority bills die at the procedural gate, not on the merits. Single limb only, final passage, per the rule this desk entered after GEO-032. Kill: the rule fails or the vote is pulled with no new date, which sends it to 25.

forecasts.q: The Houthis or an entity they control publicly institute a MANDATORY transit requirement or any charge for Bab al-Mandab passage - a published rule, not a threat, not the existing voluntary scheme
forecasts.note: OPENED at 38, and the number is deliberately BELOW the tempting analogy. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing that licenses a design read at all: the Houthi-run Humanitarian Operations Coordination Center has published a voluntary, free 'Safe Transit Request' scheme since 2025 - 48 hours notice, ship name and passage details, an answer inside a day, non-sanctioned vessels only - and on 1 August the movement explicitly DENIED any plan to charge ships, citing the UNCLOS rule that bars levying fees for mere passage. Taking Mocha, Dhubab and Perim converts that paperwork into an office. The Sound Dues logic and Iran's own PGSA, stood up within about ten weeks of gaining strait leverage, both argue yes. It is held under 50 because the counter-incentives are specific and strong: the voluntary-and-free version already buys de facto sovereignty recognition at zero diplomatic cost, which is the movement's actual product; a fee would unite Cairo, whose Suez revenue depends on the same water, with the Gulf, and would invite the naval response Washington has so far declined to mount. If it comes, it will be priced as a SERVICE - escort, pilotage, inspection - not as a toll.

forecasts.q: Russian average monthly territorial gains in Q4 2026 fall below their Q2-Q3 2026 average (ISW/DeepState)
forecasts.note: HELD at 63. ISW says neither side advanced on 11 September, and its latest assessment discusses Russian General Staff interest in roughly 800,000 additional troops. A mobilisation decree would be Michael Kofman's recruitment-versus-casualties crossover confirmed in Moscow's own paperwork - but a rumour is not a decree, and new conscripts would not reach the front in time to change fourth-quarter tempo. The seasonal base rate still supports the direction: autumn mud and winter have historically depressed mechanised advances against summer.

forecasts.q: Saudi Arabia publicly announces enrichment, weapons pursuit, or a nuclear-sharing arrangement
forecasts.note: HELD at 21. No fuel-cycle clause, reactor tender or Pakistani personnel has been reported; Saudi jets flying more than 100 raids over Yemen is the kingdom using the instruments it already owns, not a hedging document. Glenn Snyder's alliance security dilemma still frames the trend - the patron refused Riyadh's request for strikes twice - and the number stays a deliberate floor because nuclear hedging is normally covert.

forecasts.q: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, formal and holding more than 30 days
forecasts.note: HELD at 19. Peskov called a Zelenskyy-Putin meeting at the Miami G20 'impossible' but said Russia has not ruled out resuming three-way talks with the US and Ukraine in October - the Kremlin's standing thermostat language, and talks are not a ceasefire. The same day Russia struck a truck 800 metres from Poland at a supply crossing. Fortna's finding is that ceasefires hold when third parties guarantee them, and the guarantor is still what Moscow vetoes; the base rate is unchanged, with long wars sitting in the right tail where hazard rates decline.

forecasts.q: US-China tariff truce collapses before its November 2026 expiry
forecasts.note: HELD at 19. The House Rules Committee meets on Monday on the bill letting the President tariff the top buyers of Russian oil and gas, with China first among them. Drezner's sanctions paradox says a waivable threat is used first as a bargaining chip, and Xi's 24 September visit is exactly where a waiver would be traded. Nothing here moves until the procedural vote is counted.

forecasts.q: Major US and/or Israeli strike campaign on Iran resumes (multi-day, state targets)
forecasts.note: HELD at 46. The ship struck off Qeshm was Iranian, with one crew member killed - consistent with enforcement of the US blockade, which CENTCOM says has disabled four vessels, rather than a return to multi-day strikes on state targets, which is what this question needs. Marking cordon enforcement again would be the echo error. The reversal signals remain a US Treasury designation naming the Iraqi group behind the pipeline drones, or strikes on Iranian military sites lasting more than a day.

forecasts.q: Front-month Brent settles at or above $120/bbl on any daily settle before 31 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: HELD at 49 with markets shut. The weekend added Saudi raids on the Houthi-held coast and an Iranian hull hit in Hormuz, and neither changes the barrels actually loading. The IEA's cut of 2.5 million barrels a day to 2026 demand remains the counterweight: a supply shock that meets demand destruction fizzles at Stage B, and Friday's settle at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent, was the tape agreeing.

HELD at 33. No new Lebanon print this pass: the US-mediated round is still pushed to October and President Aoun still rules out talks while Israeli operations continue. Schelling's test still reads consolidation of a declared line rather than a campaign extending past it, and diplomacy receding is not the same thing as a campaign starting.

forecasts.q: Xi state visit to the US occurs in September 2026 roughly as planned
forecasts.note: HELD at 92. The BRICS summit closed normally in New Delhi and Xi remains on schedule for the White House on 24 September with no cancellation signal. Announced head-of-state visits with active sherpa preparation are consummated more than ninety per cent of the time; re-marking the same logistics fact would be the double count this ledger keeps catching.

forecasts.q: Hormuz transits recover to more than 50 per cent of pre-war volume (about 65 a day against a 130 baseline)
forecasts.note: HELD at 10 for a TENTH instance of the same pattern. President Pezeshkian told India Today the strait 'would be opened up on the condition that the U.S. will terminate its blockade' - the reopening is now explicitly hostage to the OTHER blockade, and the ship killed in Hormuz overnight was Iranian. Monday's Salalah meeting is the fourth dated venue this desk has watched; an announcement is still not a transit.

forecasts.q: IF a US-Iran or Oman Hormuz arrangement is announced by 25 Feb 2027, it preserves Iranian transit-administration machinery (the PGSA or a successor)
forecasts.note: HELD at 78 the day before Salalah. Iran says any deal would give it the right to decide which ships sail into the Gulf and possibly charge them - Iranian framing, not a Gulf signature - and Bahrain will not attend. Institutional persistence still frames it: machinery built with a named sovereignty purpose before any US deal tends to survive into the deal. A written text naming fees, permits or an Iranian administrator is the observable that would push this toward its ceiling.

forecasts.q: The US ULSD diesel crack spread settles below $45/bbl on any daily settle before 15 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: HELD at 23 with the two new facts pointing opposite ways, which is the honest reason not to mark it. Against: Petroline's terminus at Yanbu also charges the Yasref and Yanbu refineries, roughly 650,000 barrels a day of distillate-heavy Europe-facing capacity, and a crude line that is not pumping cannot feed them. For: the IEA now expects the demand losses to fall most heavily on middle distillates, which is demand destruction in the exact barrel this question prices. Diesel at the American pump is a record $6.06 a gallon against $3.71 a year ago. When the supply and demand legs of a spread move the same way, the spread does not have to.

forecasts.q: The FOMC raises the fed funds target range at or before the 9-10 December 2026 meeting
forecasts.note: HELD at 72 for a third consecutive session, and the hold is a refusal to double-count rather than an absence of news. The energy shock got worse today and the board went RED for a fourth business day, but this question turns on a sentence rather than a barrel: whether the 16 September statement drops look-through on energy, as the ECB did last week. Marking an oil headline into a rate question before the committee has spoken is exactly the error the 6 September audit caught in this question's own history.

forecasts.q: USD/JPY appreciates 8 per cent or more from its 3 September level (160.0 to 147.2 or below) in any rolling 30-day window, before 31 Mar 2027
forecasts.note: HELD at 31 with a clean data vintage for a third session. The BOJ meets on 18 September and Takata is on record that the Bank should move nimbly - a hike into a strong dollar is the mechanism that turns a funding trade into a forced unwind, which is the whole reason this question exists. Nothing in today's energy shock touches the barrier arithmetic, and marking a yen question on an oil headline is the kind of cross-contamination this book is supposed to refuse.

forecasts.q: Saudi authorities publicly confirm a force majeure at Yanbu, Jizan or Ras Tanura, OR a reduction in East-West (Petroline) throughput, before 31 Dec 2026
forecasts.note: RESOLVED YES on 12 September - Brier 0.314, the worst score on this ledger against GEO-009's 0.029, mean 0.171 across two resolutions. Kept on the board rather than retired because the post-mortem is the point: the defect was in question DESIGN, not in the world. Joining two limbs with OR meant the easy limb - any throughput reduction - carried the question, and the Ministry of Energy's precautionary shutdown announcement satisfied it within a day of opening. A question that can be resolved by a press release is not a forecast.

hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: Iranian cargo ship hit off Qeshm, one dead, on eve of Oman talks
brief.h: Iranian state media said an Iranian cargo vessel was struck before dawn on Sunday off Hengam and Qeshm islands in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one of its ten crew and wounding four - the hit UK Maritime Trade Operations logged late Saturday as an unnamed ship - while the US military, which enforces a blockade of Iranian ports, did not comment and President Masoud Pezeshkian said the strait reopens only if that blockade ends.
brief.t: Yesterday's mystery hull turns out to be Iranian, and that flips the most likely reading: not a spoiler aimed at Monday's Salalah meeting, but the other blockade at work. There are two gates in the same water - Washington's cordon around Iran's ports, which CENTCOM says has redirected 94 ships and disabled four, and Tehran's permit regime over everyone else - and each side now says its gate opens only when the other's closes. That is the whole negotiating problem in one sentence: Pezeshkian told India Today the waterway 'would be opened up on the condition that the U.S. will terminate its blockade'. Nobody has claimed the strike, so attribution stays open; what is not open is that the cargo Iran most needs to move is its own.
brief.context: EPOCH: the 1987-88 Tanker War, when both sides hit merchant shipping to squeeze the other's oil income and the US escorted reflagged Kuwaiti tankers rather than negotiate transit terms - a contest of blockades, not a battle for command of the sea. CONSTRAINT: Iran's oil revenue is near zero and its leverage is geographic, so it can only monetise the strait by formalising it - a route, an administrator, fees - and the US cordon exists to deny exactly that revenue. DESK: in Washington the blockade is a CENTCOM operation under standing orders, which is why a hull can be hit with no statement; in Tehran passage is decided by the Supreme National Security Council and the Revolutionary Guards navy, with the foreign ministry fronting Monday's meeting, which Bahrain will not attend. MECHANISM: Julian Corbett's observation that command of the sea is normally in dispute - each side polices the lanes it can reach and denies the rest, and neither needs a fleet battle to keep the other's trade shut; Nicholas Mulder's history of economic war adds that blockades squeezing a state's only export are among the most durable coercive tools on record. BASE RATE: UKMTO 'projectile' reports in this war have repeatedly gone days without public attribution, so silence is not evidence either way. FALSIFIER: a CENTCOM acknowledgement confirms enforcement; a claim by another group, or a second hit on a vessel that had cleared Iranian terms, points to a spoiler instead. A Salalah text naming fees or an Iranian administrator pushes GEO-013 (78) toward its ceiling; no text keeps GEO-001 at 10.

angles.effect: Gains a symmetry story - its closure as a reply to the US cordon - for Monday's room, and pays in its own crews and its own unmoved cargo
Keep denying Iran the revenue that would make a long closure affordable, and pay when every unattributed hit in the strait is read as theirs
Gains standing as convenor of the only regional format, and pays if its route agreement with Iran is read as endorsing permits
Pay under both regimes at once - war-risk premiums, rerouting and dead crew with nobody claiming the fire

dec.kill: A CENTCOM statement or imagery attributing the Qeshm strike, plus Monday's text: any Gulf state accepting fee or permit language in writing kills the 'two symmetric blockades' framing, because it would mean one gate is being legitimised.

consp.claim: That Iran is already enforcing its toll by force - the pinned summary of /pol/'s Persia-Israel general tells readers 'Iran strikes 3 oil tankers that were trying to bypass the Persian Gulf Strait Authority' - alongside a mirror claim that Washington could end the oil shock at once 'if america just agreed to pay iran reparations and the hormuz toll'.
consp.spread: Pinned in the OP of /pig/ #2125 (about 150 replies) and repeated in a 226-reply /pol/ thread nominally about the Ukraine talks.
consp.read: Both flatten a two-blockade contest into a single villain. The three-tanker claim is unverified by any wire this desk read, though Iran has fired at shipping during the war; the reparations line maps onto the 'war of choice' frame. The checkable fact of the day runs against the first claim: the ship that lost a crew member was Iranian.

brief.head: Saudi jets pound Houthi-held coast as Yemen's army regroups in Marib
brief.h: Saudi Arabia has flown what Al Jazeera's Sanaa correspondent counts as 129 air strikes on newly Houthi-held areas and the approaches to Marib, Yemeni government jets hit Houthi fighters on the Mocha-Dhubab road, and presidential council member Sultan al-Arada said the forces that collapsed on the west coast are regrouping in Marib and 'will return to the battle' - as the Houthis claimed a drone-and-missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Sharurah base.
brief.t: The Houthis now hold the whole Yemeni shore of the Bab al-Mandab, and the fight has moved to the two questions that decide whether that lasts: can air power deny the coast, and does Marib hold. Marib is not just a city - it is the recognised government's economic hub, sitting on the oil and gas fields that pay for what is left of the state, so a Houthi push there is a bid for revenue as well as ground. A Yemeni officer told AP he was 'stunned' the Saudi air force did nothing before Mocha fell; the raids now hitting the Mocha-Dhubab road are the first aimed at the fixed terrain the gate depends on. Donald Trump, who twice refused Riyadh's request for US strikes, said 'everything's gonna work out fine and dandy'.
brief.context: EPOCH: the 2015-22 Saudi-led air war, which ended with the Houthis still in Sanaa - and beneath it the 1970s bargain in which the kingdom outsourced hard security to a patron that has now declined to fly. CONSTRAINT: Riyadh can generate sorties in a day and cannot generate infantry that will hold a coastline; the government's ground forces answer to rival Saudi- and Emirati-funded commands, and a senior officer blamed 'lack of coordination' for the collapse. DESK: the Saudi Ministry of Defence under Khalid bin Salman runs the air campaign; any escalation beyond it sits with the royal court. MECHANISM: Robert Pape's denial-versus-punishment test - strikes on the coastal road are denial-shaped, strikes on Taiz barracks and the Marib outskirts defend ground rather than retake it. BASE RATE: air campaigns without a capable ground partner have rarely reversed territorial gains, and Yemen 2015-22 is that record written locally. INFLUENCE MAP: principal Riyadh; agents the Presidential Leadership Council factions; narrators Saba and the Houthis' al-Masirah; operator the Saudi air force; market the war-risk premium on Saudi-linked Red Sea tonnage; target Yemeni civilians - more than 500 dead in the renewed fighting and tens of thousands displaced, more than 2,000 of them to Djibouti. FALSIFIER: government forces back inside Mocha before 31 October would score against this desk's read that bombing will not reopen the coast; a Houthi breakthrough into Marib city would turn a coastal war into a resource war.

angles.effect: Buys legitimacy by promising a return to the coast, and pays heavily if a second offensive collapses the way Mocha did
Gets a Yemeni face on any counteroffensive, and pays for sorties that cannot hold ground on their own
Gains from any gap between the pledge and the front, and pays in exposed fixed positions on the coast road
Pay in displacement and air strikes in a country already classed as famine-affected

dec.kill: Government units back on the Mocha-Dhubab road in force within a month confirms al-Arada's pledge; new withdrawals from Marib's outskirts kills it.

consp.claim: That the war is really about a pipeline to Israel: a new /pol/ thread says Trump 'ghosts' the Saudis on purpose, that Riyadh's actual plan is to 'move the oil to Israel using a pipeline, and fill up tankers in the port that will be build in gaza', and that the Houthi advance was allowed to break that plan - while the /pig/ general's pinned summary insists the pipeline strike was Houthi work and that 'Saudis claim Iraqi militias' as cover.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread titled 'Trump denied air support to Saudis mercenary army' and the /pig/ general OP, about 150 replies.
consp.read: Pipeline determinism - the 'real reason is the pipeline' frame that attaches to every Gulf war. The kernel is real: Riyadh does need a route around both straits, and Saudi-Israeli land corridors have been floated for years. But no Gaza port or pipeline plan exists on the record, and Baghdad itself confirmed the drones flew from Maysan, the opposite of a Saudi cover story.

brief.head: Russian strike hits truck 800 metres from Poland's border crossing
brief.h: Russia struck a truck about 800 metres from Poland at the Dorohusk-Yahodyn crossing, briefly halting traffic, in what its Defence Ministry called a strike on infrastructure carrying 'military cargoes from Europe' - as Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called a Zelenskyy-Putin meeting at the Miami G20 'impossible' but said Russia had not ruled out resuming three-way talks with Ukraine and the US in October.
brief.t: Russia has started hitting the doors Ukraine's supplies come through, and it is doing so close enough to NATO territory that every strike carries a small chance of landing on the wrong side. That is the point of Dorohusk: raise the cost and the risk of the land bridge from Poland, where most Western weapons enter, without crossing a line anyone is obliged to answer. Both sides now run the same play - Ukrainian drones hit the refinery city of Nizhnekamsk overnight, killing two - an economic-attrition war fought on each other's logistics while envoys talk. Peskov's two sentences belong together: no summit where Zelenskyy wants one, but a door left open to an October format that Washington runs.
brief.context: EPOCH: the 2022 Western supply corridor through south-eastern Poland and the Polish-Ukrainian crossings - the logistics rail that has armed Ukraine since the invasion, now targeted at its last kilometre. CONSTRAINT: Moscow cannot strike Poland without inviting an Article 4 consultation or worse, so it strikes as close as it can; Warsaw's constraint is that a truck hit inside Ukraine is not an attack on NATO. DESK: target selection sits with the Russian General Staff; the political signal is Peskov's; the three-way format belongs to Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who said on Friday he hoped to announce 'next steps' within a couple of weeks. MECHANISM: Thomas Schelling's 'threat that leaves something to chance' - operating deliberately near a threshold so that the adversary's coalition, not just its army, carries the risk of an accident. BASE RATE: Russian drones and missile debris have strayed into Poland, Romania and Moldova repeatedly since 2022 without triggering collective defence, and the Lithuanian 'drone' that scrambled NATO jets on Sunday turned out to be a flock of birds - near-border incidents are common and escalation from them has been rare. FALSIFIER: a strike landing on Polish soil with casualties would test that base rate; a week of crossings running normally says this is harassment, not interdiction. GEO-005 holds at 19 - talks resuming is not a ceasefire.

angles.effect: Keeps a talks channel alive to steer US pressure toward Kyiv while striking the supply corridor, and so far pays nothing for the combination
Gains as the side that said yes to a meeting, and pays in logistics disruption and a winter its officials call 'very difficult', with GDP growth cut by 1.5 points
Pays in border disruption and air-defence alert costs for a war it is not formally in
Keeps a format with both capitals, and pays in credibility if its promised 'next steps' slip past September

dec.kill: A Kremlin-confirmed date and venue for an October round kills the 'talk to delay' reading; Moscow restating that any meeting must be in Moscow after a formal US invitation confirms it.

consp.claim: That Washington now blames Ukraine for the war: a 226-reply /pol/ thread opens with a Kushner quote - 'We cant have a peace agreement because Ukraine refuses to give away the territory' - with replies claiming Ukraine's population loss 'was all planned and executed', while a separate thread says a Russian mobilisation of 'around 500k men aged 20-40' is coming.
consp.spread: The Kushner thread (226 replies), a 'Kushner and Witkoff - Traitors' thread, and a smaller 'Russian mobilization rumors' thread, all on /pol/.
consp.read: The Kushner quote could not be matched to any wire this desk read - AFP has him saying only that he hoped to announce 'next steps' - so it is unverified paraphrase. The mobilisation rumour has a checkable kernel, since ISW's latest assessment discusses General Staff interest in roughly 800,000 more troops, but no decree exists. 'Planned depopulation' is a design read with no rail beneath it.

brief.head: Sweden votes with the far right bidding for its first cabinet seats
brief.h: Swedes vote on Sunday in an election polls show as nearly tied - one survey puts the left and right blocs 0.3 points apart after a record 3.6 million early votes - with the Sweden Democrats, the largest party of the governing Tidö bloc, promised key ministerial posts if the right wins; exit polls come at 20:00 local time and coalition talks are expected to take weeks or months.
brief.t: The question in Sweden is not whether the far right wins votes - it already props up the government - but whether it gets desks. For four years the Sweden Democrats traded support for policy without ministries; now they want the ministries, and for a new NATO frontline state the ones that matter are justice, migration and the defence budget. A senior Sweden Democrat went on leave after reporting linked his Russian partner to Russian state actors, and SVT traced fake 'electoral fraud' videos against the prime minister to the pro-Russian Matryoshka network - yet Swedish agencies say Moscow does not treat this election as a priority. Both can be true: interference is cheap background noise, and the decisive variable is the four per cent threshold that could knock the Liberals, and with them the right's majority, out of parliament.
brief.context: EPOCH: the post-2022 Nordic realignment - Sweden's 2024 NATO accession ended two centuries of non-alignment, and the 2022 Tidö agreement broke the cordon around the Sweden Democrats. CONSTRAINT: the four per cent threshold, which the Liberals are hovering near; if they drop out, the right loses seats without losing voters. DESK: after the count the Speaker of the Riksdag runs government formation, and a prime minister survives unless an absolute majority votes against - 'negative parliamentarism', which is why minority governments are Swedish normal. MECHANISM: Karen Stenner's authoritarian dynamic - latent preferences for order activate under perceived threat, and a campaign run on gang crime and migration is threat-activation politics. BASE RATE: European far-right parties that moved from support deals into cabinet - Austria's FPÖ in 2000 and 2017, Finland's Finns Party in 2023, the Dutch PVV in 2024 - have usually taken security or migration portfolios, and three of those four governments ended early. FALSIFIER: a left-bloc majority, or a Moderate-led government with no Sweden Democrat ministers, kills the 'desks' read; Sweden Democrats in justice or migration confirms it.

angles.effect: Gain a second term if the bloc holds, and pay by handing ministries - and responsibility for crime figures - to a party with neo-Nazi roots
Gain their first desks, and pay by becoming accountable for results they have campaigned against from outside
Gain if the Liberals fall below four per cent, and pay if a thin loss is contested by fraud narratives they did not start
Gains from polarisation at almost no cost, whichever bloc wins

dec.kill: Tonight's count and the Speaker's first round: Sweden Democrat ministers named, or a left majority. The 'not a priority target' claim fails if fraud narratives surge on a razor-thin margin.

consp.claim: That the result is set up to be stolen or staged: fabricated SVT-branded clips alleging electoral fraud against Prime Minister Kristersson circulated on X in August, and /pol/'s election-day thread calls reporting on deported migrant teenagers a 'PSYOP' because 'some of these teenagers are 21'.
consp.spread: The fake clips ran mainly on X, per SVT; the /pol/ 'Swedish Election Day' thread has about 330 replies, with a new /SEG/ general opening for the count.
consp.read: Two different objects. The fraud clips are a documented influence operation - a narrative pre-positioned for a close result, which is the tell to watch tonight if the margin is thin. The /pol/ thread also carries an ethnic-scapegoat narrative around migration and crime using nutpicking - one offender presented as a whole group; it is reported here as a phenomenon, its content not repeated.

brief.head: Bangsamoro holds first parliament vote as ex-rebel allies split
brief.h: More than 2.3 million voters in the Philippines' Bangsamoro Autonomous Region go to the polls on Monday for its first regular parliamentary election - 13 parties and nearly 700 candidates - in a contest that pits Manila-appointed interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua, running as an independent, against the machine of his former commander, MILF chairman Murad Ebrahim's United Bangsamoro Justice Party.
brief.t: This is the end of a fifty-year insurgency being tested at the ballot box, and the danger is not the old war but the new split. The Moro Islamic Liberation Front traded its guns for a self-governing region; President Marcos then replaced its chairman as chief minister with its own military chief of staff, and former comrades now run against each other through rival parties. An August 15 ambush on Macacua's convoy is still unexplained, and social-media claims that it was 'staged' show how fast perception becomes a weapon in a fragile transition. The Diplomat's analysis names the right test: not whether Monday is peaceful, but whether the losers accept the result.
brief.context: EPOCH: the 1976 Tripoli Agreement and the 2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro, which converted an armed movement into a regional government - a rail that has survived repeated postponements of this very vote. CONSTRAINT: the peace dividend depended on the MILF's organisational discipline, and electoral pluralism dissolves exactly that - former allies now sit in the UBJP and the Bangsamoro Federalist Party, which with three smaller parties backs Macacua. DESK: the Chief Minister is chosen by the new Parliament, not by voters, so the deciding desk is the chamber's coalition arithmetic - and behind it Malacañang's patronage. BASE RATE: every elected regional governor of the old ARMM from 1996 to 2013 was aligned with the sitting President, but the region's politics has always also been clan politics, and election violence here long predates the insurgency. INFLUENCE MAP: principal Manila; agent Macacua; narrators the MILF's own media and the Maguindanao clans; operator the joint ceasefire mechanisms coordinating poll security; target the former combatants deciding whether ballots still beat arms. FORECAST: this desk opened GEO-038 at 50 per cent that Macacua is elected Chief Minister before 31 December. FALSIFIER: Macacua losing his Maguindanao del Norte seat sends it toward zero; a UBJP outright majority sends it to 25; disputed results spilling into clashes involving former MILF units would put the 25 September Kuala Lumpur peace-panel meeting at risk.

angles.effect: Gains a normalised region and possibly its own appointee as elected Chief Minister, and pays if the MILF reads the result as engineered
Keep the strongest party machine, and pay in fragmentation as former commanders build rival parties
Gain parliamentary seats through dynastic networks, and carry the risk that local feuds are read as a failing peace
Gain a political stake if the vote is accepted, and are the constituency spoilers court if it is not

dec.kill: Statements by losing candidates in the week after the count, and whether the 25 September Kuala Lumpur panel meets on schedule.

consp.claim: That the 15 August ambush on interim Chief Minister Macacua's convoy was 'staged' by individuals aligned with the Bangsamoro Federalist Party - the party now backing him - to win sympathy and expose rifts inside the MILF.
consp.spread: Social-media speculation in the region, reported by The Diplomat; not seen on 4chan or the Reddit boards this session.
consp.read: A textbook false-flag frame on an unsolved attack. The checkable kernel is only that the rift is real and the investigation open. Its danger is the one the Diplomat names - in a fragile transition perception itself becomes consequential, so a disputed count could revive the claim as 'proof'.

watch: Monday's Salalah meeting: which Gulf ministers attend after Bahrain's refusal, and whether any text names fees, permits, an Iranian route administrator or the US blockade.
Attribution of the Qeshm strike - a CENTCOM statement, imagery or a claim - and whether Iran retaliates against a US-escorted hull before the talks.

lesson: Today's lesson is Thomas Schelling's 'threat that leaves something to chance', from The Strategy of Conflict (1960), and it explains why a Russian strike landed 800 metres from Poland rather than 80 kilometres inside Ukraine. Schelling noticed that a promise to start a catastrophe is rarely believed - nobody thinks a rational government will deliberately start a war it cannot win - but a RISK of catastrophe that nobody fully controls can be believed, because it does not depend on anyone choosing it. So a coercer moves toward the edge on purpose and lets the danger of an accident do the persuading: every drone aimed at a border crossing carries a small chance of hitting a Polish lorry, and that chance is carried by Poland's government and NATO's politics, not just Ukraine's army. What it predicts now is checkable: strikes on the corridor should cluster near, but not across, the frontier, and the aim is to make Warsaw and Berlin argue about the cost of the supply line, not to hit NATO. The honest caveat is Schelling's own - the technique works only while the risk stays genuinely small, and it is the one coercive tool that can produce the war nobody chose; if a strike ever kills people on Polish soil, the theory's warning, not its promise, is what came true.

quiz.q: The ship struck off Qeshm on Saturday night turned out to be Iranian. Why does that change the most likely reading of the attack?
options: It proves Iran staged the attack to win sympathy before the Oman talks
It points toward enforcement of the US blockade of Iranian ports, rather than a spoiler aimed at the talks
It shows the strait has reopened to Iranian shipping
It means the Houthis have extended their Red Sea gate into the Gulf
quiz.why: There are two blockades in the same water: the US cordon around Iran's ports and Iran's permit regime over everyone else. An Iranian hull hit in Iranian waters fits the first, though nobody has claimed it - so it is the leading reading, not a proven one.

quiz.q: Why is Marib, and not only the Red Sea coast, a prize in Yemen's renewed fighting?
options: It is the Houthis' capital
It sits on the oil and gas fields that fund the recognised government, so taking it would turn a coastal war into a fight for revenue
It is the main port for Saudi oil exports
It is where the US Navy bases its Red Sea ships
quiz.why: Marib is the government's economic hub. Controlling a chokepoint gives the Houthis leverage; controlling the state's main source of revenue would take away the other side's ability to keep fighting.

quiz.q: Russia struck a truck 800 metres from Poland. On Schelling's 'threat that leaves something to chance', what is the main purpose of striking that close to the border?
options: To attack Poland while being able to deny it
Because Russian drones cannot be aimed precisely enough to stay further away
To raise the risk and cost of the supply corridor for Ukraine's backers, without crossing the line that forces a NATO response
To test whether Polish air defences are switched on
quiz.why: Schelling's point is that a small risk of an accident nobody controls can coerce better than a threat nobody believes. Striking near the line makes Poland and NATO carry that risk - and the danger is that it can produce the war nobody chose.

quiz.q: In Monday's Bangsamoro election, why won't the vote count alone decide who becomes Chief Minister?

Only votes cast by former combatants count toward the post
quiz.why: It is a parliamentary system: voters choose members, members choose the executive. That is why the desk to watch after Monday is the chamber's arithmetic - and the patronage behind it - not just who topped the poll.

quiz.q: A commentator says: 'Swedish security agencies say Russia isn't prioritising our election, so the fake election-fraud videos don't matter.' Which observable would best test that claim?

sections.t: Saudi Arabia lost both of its roads around the Strait of Hormuz in thirty hours: drones from Iraq's Maysan province shut the East-West pipeline carrying four to five million barrels a day to Yanbu, and Houthi forces took Perim island at the mouth of Bab al-Mandab. Mohammed bin Salman asked Washington twice for strikes on the Houthis and was refused twice, receiving intelligence and targeting data instead.

The pipeline is not the story; the answer is. Since 1945 the bargain has been security for oil priced in dollars, on an unstated term: the guarantor defends the flow. Name the mechanism, the GUARANTEE LADDER - weapons, intelligence, escorts, and at the top, killing people who attack you. Clients assume they bought all of it; they bought only the rungs the guarantor's own interest will pay for. Riyadh reached for the top and was handed the third. Glenn Snyder's alliance security dilemma: a junior partner reads what its patron REFUSES more carefully than what it promises.

sections.h: Deep history I - when protection becomes tribute
sections.t: The oldest version of this ladder was built at Delos in 478 BC. The league was voluntary, aimed at Persia, and members could contribute ships or money. Most chose money, because money was convenient and crews were not. In 454 BC the treasury moved from Delos to Athens; phoros stopped meaning subscription and started meaning tribute, and some of it paid for the Parthenon. Thucydides records what became of members who tried to leave: Naxos around 470 and Thasos in 465 were besieged by the fleet they had helped finance. The guarantor prices the guarantee, and the price rises - but the sharper lesson is that the client's own convenience builds the cage. Those allies were disarmed by their preference for paying cash.

sections.h: Deep history II - real, and empty
sections.t: On 31 March 1939 Neville Chamberlain rose in the Commons and guaranteed Poland. It was formalised on 25 August as the Anglo-Polish Agreement of Mutual Assistance, carrying a secret protocol - published only after the war - that restricted the British obligation to aggression by Germany alone. So when the Red Army crossed on 17 September, Britain owed Poland precisely nothing. War was declared on 3 September; the French pushed a few miles into the Warndt forest and withdrew; Poland was finished in five weeks. The guarantee was legally genuine, publicly made and militarily undeliverable - honoured in declaration, void in relief, with the fine print written where the client could not read it.

sections.h: Deep history III - the hostage solution
sections.t: NATO was the attempt to fix that, and Article 5 repays reading slowly. Members assist by taking "such action as it deems necessary, including the use of armed force" - twelve lines where the Brussels Treaty's Article IV took four, because the US Senate would not sign automaticity. The famous clause is weaker than the clause it replaced. What made it hold for seventy-seven years was not text but Thomas Schelling's insight in Arms and Influence (1966): you cannot make a promise credible by asserting it, only by removing your own choice. American troops in West Germany and Korea, with their families, were no defence - at the Fulda Gap they would have been overrun in days. They were hostages, and a tripwire converts a future decision into an automatic consequence. Credibility bought with bodies, not adjectives. De Gaulle asked anyway - would Washington trade New York for Paris? - and answered himself with the force de frappe in 1960.

sections.h: Deep history IV - from the Quincy to Abqaiq
sections.t: On 14 February 1945, returning from Yalta, Roosevelt met Ibn Saud aboard the USS Quincy in the Great Bitter Lake. The ladder went up from there: the 1974 recycling arrangements; the Carter Doctrine of 23 January 1980, declaring an assault on the Gulf would be "repelled by any means necessary"; CENTCOM in 1983; half a million American soldiers deployed for a client state in 1991. The top rung was climbed exactly once. Then 14 September 2019: missiles and drones hit Abqaiq and Khurais and removed 5.7 million barrels a day, over half of Saudi production. The president said America was "locked and loaded," did nothing, and explained why in the sentence that has governed the Gulf ever since - that was an attack on Saudi Arabia, and it wasn't an attack on us. Seven years of Saudi behaviour follow: the Beijing-brokered normalisation with Tehran in 2023, and on 17 September 2025 the Saudi-Pakistan Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement, signed with a nuclear-armed state and left deliberately vague on whether the arsenal is included. Pakistan's defence minister said the capability "will be made available," then walked it back. The ambiguity is not sloppiness. It is the French move, performed by a client who has learned how credibility gets manufactured.

Guarantees decay from the top down: you stop striking before you stop deploying, and stop deploying before you stop selling. The rung that survives serves the guarantor's own interest - Washington kept the lane open, an American problem, and declined the land war behind it. Clients rarely defect; they dilute. Where it breaks: in 1939 Britain wanted to help and could not, in 2026 America can and will not.

Mearsheimer holds that commitments bind only where the guarantor's own survival is engaged; everything else is cheap talk - the logic of his 1993 case for Ukraine keeping its warheads. Ikenberry holds that institutionalised orders outlive the power that built them. Mearsheimer takes WHICH rungs held: the US defended the commons it consumes, not the war it doesn't. Ikenberry takes why there was no rupture: Riyadh took the intelligence and stayed. Then Schelling against Mearsheimer on the remedy - Article 5 has held over Estonia, where no American survival interest exists, because American battalions stand on it. Schelling wins the mechanism, Mearsheimer the forecast that nobody will station a tripwire in Yemen. Sagan supplies the falsifiable consequence: states build when someone else's guarantee loses credibility, not when the threat rises.

The US produces some 13.8 million barrels a day, and near eighty per cent of Hormuz crude goes to Asia: American hulls escort Chinese and Indian barrels. That subsidy to a rival will not survive twenty years of fiscal stress in a country whose debt service exceeds its defence budget - Kennedy's overstretch, or more precisely Gilpin's rising protection costs. By 2035 the American Gulf posture converts from insurance into a fee-and-arms business: about 60 per cent. Bolder: at least one Gulf state holds an overt or thinly-veiled latent nuclear capability by 2035, about 55 per cent. Our twelve-month ledger line on a Saudi announcement is 21 per cent, and a floor: hedging is covert, so watch reactor tenders for a fuel-cycle clause. Counterweight: announced after Suez and after Saigon too. Disconfirmers: US strikes on the Houthis within sixty days, or a ratified treaty with Riyadh.

Glenn Snyder, Alliance Politics (1997) - the abandonment-entrapment dilemma. - Thomas Schelling, Arms and Influence (1966), ch. 2-3 - why a tripwire beats a treaty. - Scott Sagan, "Why Do States Build Nuclear Weapons?" (International Security, 1996).
